Fowler, Mariantoni, Martinis & Cleland, 'Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation' (arXiv v2, posted 2012-10-27): factoring a 2000-bit (600-digit) number at an error rate about one-tenth of threshold (p = 10^-3 in App. M) 'the full quantum computer needs about a billion physical qubits, operating for about one day'. Verifier correction: the staged row paired v1's date (2012-08-04) with v2's figure; v1 stated 'about 220 million physical qubits', so date/source moved to v2. 2000-bit, not exactly 2048: Gidney & Ekerå 2019 (arXiv:1905.09749, Table) list Fowler et al. 2012 as the n=2048 estimate at 0.1% error with 1000 million qubits

Gheorghiu & Mosca, 'Benchmarking the quantum cryptanalysis of symmetric, public-key and hash-based cryptographic schemes' (arXiv v1 2019-02-06): RSA-2048 at physical error rate per gate 10^-3, 'Approximately 1.72 x 10^8 physical qubits are required to break the scheme in one day'

Gidney & Ekerå, 'How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits' (arXiv v1 2019-05-23; Quantum 5, 433, 2021): physical gate error 10^-3, 1 us surface-code cycle, 10 us reaction time

Gidney, 'How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits' (arXiv v1 2025-05-21): 'less than a million noisy qubits', less than a week, uniform gate error 0.1%; 'less than N' recorded as N

Webster et al. (Iceberg Quantum), 'The Pinnacle Architecture: Reducing the cost of breaking RSA-2048 to 100 000 physical qubits using quantum LDPC codes' (arXiv v1 2026-02-12): 'fewer than one hundred thousand physical qubits, given a physical error rate of 10^-3' (qLDPC codes, assumes non-local connectivity; ~1 month runtime); 'fewer than N' recorded as N

Quantinuum H1-1 (20 fully connected qubits per the System Model H1 spec page): 99.914(3)% two-qubit gate fidelity averaged over all five gate zones, all zones >99.9%, 'across all qubit pairs' on the commercial system; first full commercial device at >=99.9%

Quantinuum Helios launch: 98 fully connected physical qubits, two-qubit gate fidelity 99.921% 'across all qubit pairs' (benchmark paper arXiv 2511.05465: average 2Q infidelity 7.9(2)e-4 over all operational zones; an average, not a median)

White, Southgate, Thomson & Brenner, 'The structure of the nervous system of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans', Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 314:1-340 (12 Nov 1986): 'The hermaphrodite nervous system has a total complement of 302 neurons' with ~5000 chemical synapses, 2000 NMJs, 600 gap junctions

La-Ba-Cu-O: first claim Bednorz & Müller, Z. Phys. B 64, 189 (June 1986, onset 'in the 30 K range', resistivity only); independent confirmation with both susceptibility and resistivity by Takagi, Uchida, Kitazawa & Tanaka, Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 26, L123 (Feb 1987 issue): 'Tc near 30 K'. Beats the pre-window Nb3Ge record (~23 K)

Y-Ba-Cu-O: first claim Wu, Chu et al., PRL 58, 908 (2 Mar 1987, 'transition between 80 and 93 K', resistive and magnetic); independent confirmation Cava et al. (Bell Labs), 'Bulk superconductivity at 91 K in single-phase oxygen-deficient perovskite Ba2YCu3O9-δ', PRL 58, 1676 (20 Apr 1987) = earliest independent confirmation verified here (others may predate it by weeks). La-Sr-Cu-O (36 K, Jan 1987) not staged: its independent confirmation not verified

Bi-based cuprates: first claim Maeda et al., Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 27, L209 (Feb 1988, 'Tc of about 105 K'); independent report Chu et al. (Houston), 'Superconductivity up to 114 K in the Bi-Al-Ca-Sr-Cu-O compound system without rare-earth elements', PRL 60, 941 (7 Mar 1988); family-level confirmation (Al-containing composition), value = onset per title

Tl-Ba-Ca-Cu-O: first claim Sheng & Hermann, Nature 332, 138 (Mar 1988, onset 120 K, zero resistance above 100 K); independent IBM report Parkin et al., 'Bulk superconductivity at 125 K in Tl2Ca2Ba2Cu3Ox', PRL 60, 2539 (13 Jun 1988), zero resistance at ~125 K

Hg-1223: first claim Schilling, Cantoni, Guo & Ott, Nature 363, 56 (6 May 1993; magnetic and resistive, max Tc ~133 K); independent Houston group (Chu et al., Nature 365, 323, 23 Sep 1993): 'Single-phase Hg-1223 was subsequently synthesized and found to be superconducting at a record temperature of 135 K' (citing Huang et al., Physica C in press). Verifier: removed the unsourced 138 K (Tl/F-doped Hg-1223) remark; the 151 K pressure-quenched Hg-1223 result (PNAS, 9 Mar 2026, Chu group) is not counted here as no independent report is cited
